summary: The unnamed Vault 13 resident sent to recover a water chip, tasked with ending the mutant threat and exiled after defeating the Unity.
description: Fallout leaves the Vault Dweller's personal name, sex, route and exact completion dates open. The record therefore follows mission structure and supported relationships rather than inventing a single playthrough.

articleSections.title: A resident of Vault 13
paragraphs: The protagonist begins as a member of a sealed community that has remained underground for roughly eighty years. The game supplies no canonical personal name and allows the player to define sex, abilities and conduct.
That openness is part of the lore model: 'Vault Dweller' is a role and descriptive title, not evidence for a fixed biography imported from one playthrough.

articleSections.title: The water-chip mission
paragraphs: The Overseer sends the Dweller toward Vault 15 after Vault 13's purification controller fails. The eventual replacement comes through the water system beneath Necropolis, but the route, detours and completion date vary.
Returning the chip resolves the immediate mechanical crisis and triggers a second mission rather than ending the journey.

articleSections.title: Conflict with Unity
paragraphs: The successful route eliminates both Mariposa's production vats and the Master beneath the Cathedral. Fallout permits either order and several methods, so the archive records common outcomes without selecting a canonical tactical path.

articleSections.title: Return and exile
paragraphs: The Overseer praises the returning hero but refuses readmission, arguing that younger Vault residents would imitate the Dweller and leave. The decision turns the saviour of Vault 13 into an exile in order to preserve the Vault's closed political order.
The player may leave or kill the Overseer. Exile is shared by both final variants; the Overseer's survival is conditional.

summary: The isolated mountain Vault whose water-purification controller failure begins Fallout and whose population faces dehydration or Unity discovery in failure branches.
description: Vault 13 is both a technological system and a closed society. Its survival depends on repair, secrecy and an Overseer willing to exile the person who preserved it.

articleSections.title: A closed mountain community
paragraphs: Vault residents describe a community that has remained below ground for about eighty years. Hydroponics, security, medical and technical roles support daily life, while unrest is treated as a threat to collective survival.
The Overseer's final decision shows that isolation is political as well as physical: contact with the outside can destabilise the social order even when it saves the population.

articleSections.title: Water-chip failure
paragraphs: The Vault's purification controller fails shortly before 5 December 2161. The Overseer says local workshops cannot manufacture the replacement and stored water is finite.
Hub water deliveries can extend the deadline but impose continuing expense and the risk that caravans reveal the Vault's location.

articleSections.title: Two missions
paragraphs: The first mission seeks a compatible chip, initially using Vault 15 as the lead. After its return, the Overseer sends the Dweller against the source of an artificially produced mutant army.

articleSections.title: Conditional failure states
paragraphs: If the water deadline expires, the population dies from deprivation. If Unity locates the Vault, super mutants invade. These are mutually exclusive failure branches, not events that occur on the successful route.

summary: A guarded, irrigated and mostly self-sufficient settlement led by Aradesh, connected to Vault 15 through Katrina but not proven by Fallout alone to have an entirely Vault 15-derived founding population.
description: Shady Sands combines subsistence agriculture, local medicine, raider pressure and conditional futures that range from NCR emergence to destruction.

articleSections.title: Settlement and economy
paragraphs: Shady Sands maintains gardens, a well, irrigation and brahmin while relying on barter and scavenging. Guards and an inward-looking leadership protect a community vulnerable to radscorpions and raiders.

articleSections.title: Vault 15 connection and its limits
paragraphs: Katrina is a Vault 15 survivor who lives in Shady Sands. Jarvis says an ancestor of Aradesh founded the settlement, but does not identify that founder's origin.
Fallout therefore establishes a migration connection without establishing the later, broader claim that every founder descended from Vault 15.

articleSections.title: Radscorpions and Khans
paragraphs: Radscorpions threaten residents and livestock; Razlo studies their poison. The Khans create a second crisis by abducting Tandi, drawing the Vault Dweller into a method-variable rescue.

articleSections.title: Conditional futures
paragraphs: The most favourable ending has Aradesh and Tandi guide Shady Sands into the New California Republic. Other branches remove either leader, place Tandi in sole authority, produce a council followed by raider destruction, or end in mutant invasion.
The NCR origin is therefore a Fallout ending possibility. Later continuity can select and elaborate a branch, but it should not make every Fallout ending simultaneous.

summary: A multi-district trade centre built around caravan companies, water distribution, policing, organised crime and sharp inequality.
description: The Hub connects regional commerce to the Unity plot: what begins as a missing-caravan mystery becomes evidence of captive screening and forced conversion.

articleSections.title: Districts and inequality
paragraphs: Downtown forms the caravan and merchant core. The Heights are affluent, Old Town is poor, and the Water Merchants operate to the south. This social geography underlies Loxley's redistributive claims and Decker's protection network.

articleSections.title: Water and caravans
paragraphs: Water Merchants control the main supply and can contract deliveries to Vault 13. Crimson Caravan and Far Go Traders connect settlements across dangerous routes, while caps circulate as Hub-backed money in Katrina's account.

articleSections.title: Missing caravans and Unity
paragraphs: Three Far Go caravans disappear in a month. Mutant Transmissions reveals that Unity scavengers capture travellers, assess contamination and forward viable people to the Lieutenant for processing at Mariposa.

articleSections.title: Crime, policing and Harold
paragraphs: Decker's Underground operates from the Maltese Falcon through extortion and killings; Justin Greene can act against it. Loxley leads a competing thieves' organisation in Old Town.
Harold supplies the city's deeper historical connection to Richard Grey and Mariposa, while his possible ending links personal treatment to a more egalitarian Hub.

articleSections.title: Conditional endings
paragraphs: One ending connects kindness toward Harold to a more equal Hub. A mutant advance causes residents to disperse in another. Many neutral state combinations receive no slide and should not be converted into invented outcomes.

summary: The bombed ruins of Los Angeles, containing Adytum, the Blades, Followers, Gun Runners, deathclaw territory and the Cathedral complex.
description: The Boneyard is a network of communities rather than a single government, with political, industrial, humanitarian and religious organisations occupying distinct sites.

articleSections.title: Angel's Boneyard and Los Angeles
paragraphs: Fallout dialogue explicitly equates Angel's Boneyard with the ruins of Los Angeles. Adytum, the Blades, Followers Library and Gun Runners factory form a connected but politically fragmented region.

articleSections.title: Adytum and Regulator control
paragraphs: Jon Zimmerman is the public leader, but the Regulators hold coercive power. Caleb's internal transmission proves he ordered Josh Zimmerman's murder and a frame-up of the Blades.

articleSections.title: Gun Runners and deathclaws
paragraphs: Gun Runners manufacture arms at a fixed industrial site and depend on Adytum materials after exhausting local scrap. A reproducing deathclaw nest blocks access and makes relocation difficult.

articleSections.title: Followers and Cathedral investigation
paragraphs: Nicole's Followers preserve knowledge, advocate peace and investigate the Children. Laura's infiltration ties the Boneyard's humanitarian network to the concealed Unity structure beneath the Cathedral.

summary: A Boneyard educational and humanitarian organisation founded by Nicole around peace, preserved knowledge and resistance to another cycle of war.
description: The Followers combine teaching and medical aid with investigation of the Children; their survival and future influence are conditional in Fallout's endings.

articleSections.title: Formation and mission
paragraphs: Nicole formed the organisation after migration and violence killed her parents. The group preserves knowledge, teaches peace and tries to prevent another catastrophe.

articleSections.title: Investigation of the Children
paragraphs: Nicole suspects the Children after dissidents disappear. Laura infiltrates the Cathedral and reports concealed access used by Nightkin.

articleSections.title: Conditional outcomes
paragraphs: With support and without invasion, the Followers become an important Boneyard influence. In the invasion branch they are destroyed by mutant forces. Neither future is unconditional.

summary: The Master's coercive movement and army, using the Children as a public front and Mariposa to convert selected humans into super mutants.
description: Unity combines an anti-war ideal of ending difference with forced conversion, planned sterilisation, killing of resisters and a search for uncontaminated Vault populations.

articleSections.title: Ideology and policy
paragraphs: The Master claims that a single mutant race can end the human divisions that caused nuclear war. Unity policy turns that premise into compulsory transformation and political domination.

articleSections.title: Children, army and command
paragraphs: The Children provide hospitals, missionaries and a public theology. Nightkin guard concealed functions, the Lieutenant commands Mariposa and the Master directs the whole project beneath the Cathedral.

articleSections.title: Captive and Vault search network
paragraphs: Scavenger teams abduct caravan travellers, assess their contamination and forward useful captives to Mariposa. Vault populations are especially valuable because low-radiation subjects tend to produce better mutants.

articleSections.title: Loss of the Master and vats
paragraphs: The successful route destroys both the Cathedral command centre and the Mariposa production vats. Ending narration says the surviving armies flee east after losing leader and reinforcement source.
The order of the two targets varies, so the archive models a shared strategic result rather than two simultaneous versions.

articleSections.title: Lost Hills in 2161
paragraphs: By 2161 the Brotherhood is governed by elders under High Elder John Maxson. Rhombus leads military training, Vree represents scientific work, Talus handles Paladin matters and Cabbot meets outsiders at the entrance.
Scribes preserve and design, Knights manufacture and maintain, and Paladins protect the organisation. The Brotherhood trades for food and supplies while restricting access to its bunker.

articleSections.title: The mutant threat
paragraphs: John Maxson suspects an organised mutant army, but the council initially requires evidence. The Vault Dweller can supply proof and secure Paladin support against Unity targets.

articleSections.title: Contradictory ending branches
paragraphs: A favourable ending presents restrained aid, research and reintroduction of technology without direct rule. A hostile branch produces the Steel Plague, a techno-religious dictatorship.
The outcomes are explicitly mutually exclusive and should not be used as a timeless definition of the faction.

articleSections.title: The bunker in 2161
paragraphs: Fallout presents Lost Hills as a multi-level headquarters with entrance control, training, manufacturing, medical, library and council functions. Its internal geography expresses the division between military, technical and political work.

articleSections.title: Outsiders and initiation
paragraphs: The Brotherhood is cautious toward outsiders. Cabbot directs an applicant to the lethally irradiated Glow, echoing the earlier Dennis Allen expedition while turning retrieval into an initiation test.

description: The Glow is both a lethal post-War ruin and the archive that preserves West Tek's research history through ZAX, laboratories and holodisks.

articleSections.title: The West Tek research facility
paragraphs: Before the Great War the site hosted biological work alongside physics, laser and power-armour programmes. ZAX records initialization in 2053, biological research from 2055 and military control from 2071.

articleSections.title: PIV and FEV evidence
paragraphs: ZAX and recovered disks trace cure research into PIV and FEV, escalating animal trials and the January 2077 transfer to Mariposa. The records distinguish established observations from ZAX's own conjectures.

articleSections.title: Brotherhood expeditions
paragraphs: Dennis Allen's expedition reached the irradiated ruins and lost members to radiation and security systems despite power armour. In 2161 Cabbot uses the same destination as an outsider initiation task.

articleSections.title: Unity production centre in 2161
paragraphs: By 2161 Unity occupies Mariposa and uses the former research base as its principal conversion centre. The Lieutenant commands detention, interrogation and the FEV vats while field teams send screened captives for processing.
This later occupation extends the site's history without replacing the 2077 rebellion and exodus already documented by the archive.

articleSections.title: Destruction of mutant production
paragraphs: Neutralising the vats is required on the successful route because it removes Unity's ability to create new troops. The exact infiltration or combat method and its calendar date are player-dependent.

articleSections.title: Transmission and transformation
paragraphs: ZAX describes the tested agent as requiring injection or direct contact rather than airborne spread. It rewrites damaged or intact DNA with outcomes that depend heavily on the subject.

articleSections.title: Radiation and outcome quality
paragraphs: The scientific records connect radiation-damaged genomes with failed or poor transformations. The Lieutenant reaches a similar practical conclusion through a different, disputed explanation about wasteland exposure.

articleSections.title: Sterility evidence and limits
paragraphs: Vree directly observes atrophied reproductive anatomy and no viable sperm in examined mutants. ZAX's proposed gamete-repair mechanism is explicitly conjectural, while the Lieutenant calls sterility temporary.
The archive therefore distinguishes anatomical evidence, causal hypothesis and contradicted operational claim.
